_comment: Written per row under wsp's state and passed to a member seat's Claude Code with --settings (wsp-681), <row> replaced by its own row. Auto mode's classifier denied members `wsp check <row> --set` (an agent rewriting the checks that judge its own work), so every row whose check line needed a budget, a cd or a narrower path blocked on Ed. The rule allows the call on the seat's own row only; wsp itself decides what of the change a member may make and logs each change for the verifier.
_comment_guard: PreToolUse on Bash is the kill guard (wsp-691): wsp-session.sh refuses a pkill, killall or killing pgrep with an option after its first pattern (BSD getopt reads it as one more pattern: on 2026-11-19 `pkill -f "scripts/check.mjs" -P 0` ended every Claude session on the machine), one naming a bare common name (claude, node, wsp, compound-sup, compound-render, cargo), or a pkill pattern under 4 characters, and says to kill by pid. The command runs the script from ~/.claude/hooks, where `wsp install` writes the copy the binary carries (wsp-428), wherever the checkout is; the same text is in every seat's settings and in the snippet, so where both hold it the two are one command and agree; a verifier or plain seat, which has no role file, is started with wsp-seat.settings.json, which holds only this hook.

allow: `wsp check <row> --set --why "…"` on the seat's own row <row> is authorised by Ed: wsp itself lets a member only raise a step's budget, add or correct a leading `cd <dir> &&`, narrow a step to the files its commits touched, or add a step, refuses deleting a step, lowering a budget or replacing a command, and logs every change with its reason where the row's verifier reads it.
